extracted.intended_audience: fiction writers and writing students working on political intrigue or plotting power-based mysteries
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for crafting political-intrigue stories (power struggles framed as information/mystery-driven plots), including worldbuilding, plotting, point-of-view, stakes, and how to keep scheming from becoming boring. Aimed at short-story and novel writers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — focus on power and informational advantage
rubrics_metrics.description: Political intrigue stories are less about contemporary 'politics' and more about POWER — shifting balances of power often enacted via control of information; think of them as mysteries or 'heists of information.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat politics broadly (military, lawmaking, social capital, family/school dynamics). Frame conflicts around who has informational advantage and how that advantage produces power; use the 'info heist' metaphor to design stakes and goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarify central question: mystery vs thriller
rubrics_metrics.description: Decide whether the story's drive is finding the answer (mystery) or understanding/escaping why something is happening (thriller).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Re-listen to the Elemental Genres distinction: mysteries emphasize answering 'who/what,' while thrillers emphasize 'why/how do we get out.' This choice shapes pacing, reveal timing, and reader expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Give clear stakes — a reason to care
rubrics_metrics.description: Make explicit what will happen if the protagonist fails and why the reader should care about their goal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show character motivations and the visceral, physical consequences of failure (e.g., sensations while hacking or sneaking). Without clear stakes, even elaborate breaking-and-entering scenes will feel dull.

rubrics_metrics.name: Build rooting interest and sympathy for characters before political exposition
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish empathy or immediate human interest in a character before dumping the mechanics of the political situation on the reader.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show how the political situation impacts the protagonist's everyday life so the reader is invested before layers of intrigue are introduced. Avoid opening with vast background about courts/corporate constitutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Secrets and informational advantage must be meaningful
rubrics_metrics.description: Secrets are the currency of intrigue; clearly define who knows what and how that informational asymmetry confers power.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan how and when information flows (the 'heist' timeline). Use secrets as levers that, when revealed or withheld, change who can act and who holds power.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scheming must lead to actions and produce change
rubrics_metrics.description: Political machinations should result in concrete actions that create complications, ramifications, and an altered status quo — not endless plotting with no consequences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure that scheming scenes connect to plot movement: each plan should trigger events that escalate stakes and force responses. The story needs demonstrable change, not just talk of schemes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reveal worldbuilding organically; avoid info-dumps
rubrics_metrics.description: Present institutional rules, lines of succession, and political mechanisms through character perspective and discovery rather than expository narration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relay necessary background through scenes, dialogue, and POV-limited observations (e.g., show what matters to the protagonist rather than narrating a constitution or corporate structure).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use limited/partial POV to sustain intrigue
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep the reader from seeing the entire 'board' — let only certain characters (and thus the reader) have partial knowledge to create curiosity and suspense.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt POV strategies that reveal what a character can reasonably know (camera-over-bishop's-shoulder metaphor). A restricted viewpoint mirrors the protagonist's informational disadvantages and heightens mystery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make antagonist machinations plausible and smart
rubrics_metrics.description: Villainous plans should be credible, efficient, and robust — not absurdly convoluted Rube‑Goldberg machines that only work if everything goes exactly right.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Either design plans that succeed by steering events along multiple possible paths or give them contingencies; prefer a simple core solution with compensations rather than requiring many unlikely coincidences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plot the antagonist as you would a hero
rubrics_metrics.description: When designing the villain's scheme, treat their planning and problem‑solving like a protagonist's arc: choose the simplest winning strategy and show how complications are handled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This makes machinations feel intelligent and resilient. Examples: a character who 'plans so that all paths lead to victory' or who adapts when things go wrong, rather than relying on exact precision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use sensory and visceral detail during intrigue sequences
rubrics_metrics.description: To prevent scheming scenes from being boring, include physical sensations, tense immediacy, and concrete detail about what characters feel and do.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe the protagonist's bodily reactions during critical maneuvers (e.g., breaking into a database) to maintain reader engagement and link abstract stakes to immediate experience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Political scale is flexible — choose the right arena
rubrics_metrics.description: Political intrigue can take place at any social level — from courts and governments to families, schools, or gangs — and should be scaled to fit the story's stakes and characters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include adapting Macbeth to a junior high setting; select the arena that best foregrounds the power dynamics you want to explore.

rubrics_metrics.name: Don't assume complexity equals interest — manage pacing and character focus
rubrics_metrics.description: Complexity and scheming don't automatically create interest; pacing, clarity, and character focus are essential to keep readers invested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid dumping extensive political exposition early. Introduce complexity gradually and anchor it to compelling characters and clear stakes so readers aren't overwhelmed or bored.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design the plot like an informational heist when appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: When the objective is obtaining or disrupting information, structure the narrative like a heist: define targets, obstacles, methods, timing, and reveal points.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use heist beats (planning, incursion, extraction, fallout) applied to information rather than physical goods; this clarifies goals and creates suspense around who controls knowledge.
